data.narrative:
Standard Nuclear, a public-stage nuclear energy company founded by Kurt Terrani, has raised $332M+ across private and public markets ($182M private, $150M IPO). The nuclear energy sector comp universe includes 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private competitors, anchored by five leading private firms: Oklo, X-Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

The peer-median approach is inapplicable here due to insufficient narrow peer set depth. Of the 6 same-sector peers identified, none satisfy concurrent filtering on stage, adjacency, or valuation tier—a minimum threshold of 3 datapoints is required. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias given the sector's heterogeneity in technology maturity, regulatory pathway, and capital intensity. As a result, no triangulated valuation range can be supported by the available quantitative methods.

This analysis underscores a structural constraint: Standard Nuclear occupies a sparse competitive landscape where traditional comparable-company analysis lacks adequate statistical foundation. Resolution would require either (1) identifying additional same-stage or adjacent-stage nuclear peers with disclosed valuations, (2) constructing bottom-up DCF assumptions anchored to project-level economics, or (3) applying precedent transaction analysis if M&A or financing data exists. Without these inputs, a defensible valuation estimate cannot be derived from peer triangulation alone.
